project.name: planevacuation

nodes.name: getIconImageSource

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the root README to understand SecurPlan's purpose, its Django and Next.js split, and the local workflow for running both halves. Its route inventory and verification commands provide the map for the end-to-end editor journey that follows.

tour.title: Runtime Foundations
tour.description: With the project map in hand, follow the two runtime foundations: Django management commands enter through manage.py, while the Next.js root layout establishes the frontend shell and shared authentication state. Django settings then connects applications, middleware, JWT authentication, storage, CORS, and the development database into the backend runtime.
tour.languageLesson: Django centralizes runtime behavior in a settings module selected by its management entry point, while a Next.js App Router layout composes providers and shared UI around every nested route.

tour.title: Authenticated Plan Intake
tour.description: Building on those runtime foundations, the authentication context manages JWT-backed identity and supplies credentials to the client, while the API helper consistently targets the Django origin. The new-plan page uses those services to submit an image or PDF with site metadata, then sends the user into the editor after the backend creates the plan.
tour.languageLesson: React Context provides shared authentication state without threading it through every component, and hooks coordinate token persistence, user loading, and route-level side effects.

tour.title: Editor Orchestration
tour.description: Once a plan exists, the dynamic editor route becomes the feature's control center. It coordinates loading and saving, editing tools, undo and redo, cropping and cleaning, secondary plans, asynchronous xAI jobs, navigation safeguards, and high-resolution export, making it the best place to see how the whole workflow is assembled.

tour.title: Interactive Canvas Model
tour.description: The editor delegates spatial interaction to PlanCanvas, which renders backgrounds, overlays, safety pictograms, text, lines, shapes, polygon zones, transforms, and printable sheet layouts with React Konva. The safety-icon catalogue supplies normalized visual behavior, while sheet templates define the regulatory blocks and plan window used to compose a printable evacuation sheet.
tour.languageLesson: React Konva expresses a canvas scene as React components, but pointer gestures and transforms still require careful synchronization between mutable canvas nodes and serializable application state.

tour.title: REST API Boundary
tour.description: The canvas state crosses into Django through the project and application URL configurations, which expose authentication, plan, pictogram, icon, and media routes. Views enforce authenticated behavior and perform editor synchronization and image processing, while serializers validate and translate the nested plan entities exchanged with the frontend.
tour.languageLesson: Django REST Framework separates routing, request handling, and serialization: routers select a view, views enforce workflow rules, and serializers validate API data against Python objects.

tour.title: Persistence and Cleaning
tour.description: Behind the API boundary, the models persist plans together with icons, overlays, shapes, text, cleaning history, jobs, and per-user service credentials. The initial migration establishes that schema, the overlay migration shows how support for multiple secondary plans evolved, and the Grok cleaning service turns uploaded plans into normalized architectural backgrounds while presenting stable errors to the editor.
tour.languageLesson: Django migrations record ordered schema changes separately from the current model definitions, allowing database structure and application code to evolve together.

tour.title: Verification and Contracts
tour.description: After tracing the full data path, use the backend integration suite to verify registration, JWT flows, plan CRUD, PDF uploads, image cleaning, history, credentials, and asynchronous jobs at the API boundary. The frontend's strict TypeScript configuration complements those runtime tests by checking the editor and shared client code without emitting build artifacts.
tour.languageLesson: Integration tests protect behavior across routing, serialization, persistence, and services, while TypeScript's no-emit checking treats the compiler as a static contract verifier rather than a build step.

tour.title: Export and Deployment
tour.description: Finish at the delivery boundary: ExportButtons presents PNG and PDF choices, including paper format, on top of the editor's high-resolution export pipeline. The frontend package manifest supplies the Konva, PDF, styling, build, and lint toolchain, while the backend requirements capture Django, PostgreSQL, OpenCV, PDF, and external-service support. Next.js and environment configuration complete the production path by defining the frontend build root and the browser-visible backend API origin.
tour.languageLesson: A NEXT_PUBLIC_ environment variable is embedded for browser-side access in Next.js, so it should contain a public API origin rather than a secret; deployment manifests must keep private credentials on the server side.
